q_criterion.definition: Q = 0.5*(||Ω||² - ||S||²) where Ω is rotation-rate tensor and S is strain-rate tensor
q_criterion.interpretation: Q > 0 indicates regions where rotation dominates strain, identifying vortex cores
q_criterion.typical_use: Visualizing coherent vortical structures like wingtip vortices, C-pillar vortices, A-pillar vortices

vorticity.interpretation: High vorticity indicates strong rotation, but includes shear layers (not purely vortices)
vorticity.typical_use: Quick identification of rotational regions, less selective than Q-criterion

lambda2.interpretation: λ₂ < 0 identifies vortex cores more precisely than Q-criterion, excludes shear
lambda2.typical_use: Accurate vortex core identification, more expensive to compute

vortex_isosurface.threshold_guidance: Higher threshold shows stronger/tighter vortex cores, lower threshold shows weaker/larger structures
vortex_isosurface.coloring_guidance: Color by velocity magnitude to see flow speed through vortex, or by pressure to see vortex-induced pressure drop

streamlines.interpretation: Shows flow direction and path. In wake region, reveals recirculation, entrainment, and vortex structure
streamlines.seed_placement: Seeding downstream of body captures wake development. Seed radius controls coverage.
streamlines.coloring_guidance: Color by velocity magnitude to identify acceleration/deceleration, or by pressure for pressure recovery

locations.wake: Slice normal to flow direction, positioned downstream of body, shows wake cross-section
locations.center: Slice through domain center, shows overall flow field

interpretation.velocity: Low velocity regions indicate wake deficit, flow separation, or stagnation
interpretation.pressure: Low pressure indicates suction (upper surface, vortex cores), high pressure indicates stagnation

histogram.description: Distribution of field values across the domain

interpretation.pressure: Peak location indicates dominant pressure level. Wide distribution suggests large pressure variation. Bimodal distribution may indicate separation.
interpretation.velocity: Peak near freestream indicates attached flow. Lower peak indicates wake/separated region contribution.

force_distribution.description: Sectional and accumulated force along body axis
force_distribution.interpretation: Shows where forces are generated. Sectional force peaks indicate high-load regions. Accumulated force shows running total.
force_distribution.design_relevance: Identifies which body sections contribute most to drag/lift. Useful for targeting geometry changes.

boundary_layer.description: Velocity profile normal to body surface
boundary_layer.interpretation: Shows velocity development from zero at wall to freestream. Profile shape indicates laminar vs turbulent flow.

metrics.delta: Boundary layer thickness - distance where u/U∞ = 0.99
metrics.delta_star: Displacement thickness δ* = ∫(1 - u/U∞)dy - represents mass flow deficit due to BL
metrics.theta: Momentum thickness θ = ∫(u/U∞)(1 - u/U∞)dy - represents momentum deficit, directly related to drag
metrics.shape_factor: H = δ*/θ, indicates flow state: H ≈ 2.6 (laminar), H ≈ 1.3-1.4 (turbulent), H > 3 suggests separation

boundary_layer.design_relevance: Thin BL = less drag, thick BL = more momentum loss. High H suggests separation risk. θ growth rate indicates skin friction drag.
